record.paper_title: Multi-Head Finite Automata: Characterizations, Concepts and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Conversion bounds between one-head data-independent and data-dependent automata
record.original_question: Determine tight conversion bounds between one-head data-independent finite automata and one-head data-dependent finite automata. In particular, when a language is recognized by a one-head data-independent finite automaton, what description-size blow-up is required to convert it into an equivalent one-head data-dependent deterministic, nondeterministic, or alternating finite automaton, and what bounds hold in the reverse direction?

evidence.quote: We close this subsection by mentioning some open problems for further research: (1) Determine the bounds of the conversions of one-head data-independent finite automata into one-head data-dependent deterministic, nondeterministic, and alternating finite automata and vice versa.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A one-head finite automaton is a finite automaton (deterministic, nondeterministic, or alternating) that reads its input via a single head moving on a tape containing the input word. Such an automaton is called data-independent (or oblivious) if the sequence of head positions during a computation depends only on the length of the input word and not on the specific symbols of the input; otherwise it is called data-dependent. The description size of an automaton is measured by its total number of states (or by the total length of a standard encoding of its transition function).

For each pair (X, Y) with X ∈ {data-independent} and Y ∈ {data-dependent deterministic, data-dependent nondeterministic, data-dependent alternating} (and the analogous pairs in the reverse direction), determine tight upper and lower bounds on the description-size blow-up needed to convert a one-head finite automaton of type X recognizing a language L into an equivalent one-head finite automaton of type Y recognizing the same language. That is, find a function f(n) such that every type-X automaton with n states can be converted to an equivalent type-Y automaton with at most f(n) states, and exhibit a family of languages witnessing that this bound cannot be improved (up to constants), for each of the six conversion directions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open problem in the survey on multi-head finite automata by Holzer, Kutrib, and Malcher. Related work (Holzer, MFCS 1997; later papers on data-independent vs. data-dependent multi-head automata, and on tight hierarchies of data-independent multi-head automata) studies the broader k-head setting and shows that many conversions yield non-recursive trade-offs, but no published source found in the search establishes tight conversion bounds for the one-head data-independent vs. data-dependent case. Status could not be confirmed from the available sources.
